Interface RequestCondition

All Known Implementing Classes:
RequestCondition.AllOf, RequestCondition.AnyOf, RequestCondition.Body, RequestCondition.Cookie, RequestCondition.Custom, RequestCondition.Header, RequestCondition.Host, RequestCondition.Method, RequestCondition.Not, RequestCondition.PeerAddress, RequestCondition.Query, RequestCondition.RemoteAddress, RequestCondition.TimeWindow
public sealed interface RequestCondition permits RequestCondition.Header, RequestCondition.Query, RequestCondition.Cookie, RequestCondition.Method, RequestCondition.Host, RequestCondition.RemoteAddress, RequestCondition.PeerAddress, RequestCondition.TimeWindow, RequestCondition.AllOf, RequestCondition.AnyOf, RequestCondition.Not, RequestCondition.Custom, RequestCondition.Body<T>
A declarative condition on a request, for RouteSpec.where(RequestCondition): on its headers, query parameters, cookies, method, host, client and peer addresses and the time it arrives, and their combinations. A condition is data: the router reads it, flattens and orders it cheapest first when the route is built, and shows it in the route info, which a lambda does not allow. custom(Predicate) takes a lambda for what the others do not express. 
import static io.micronaut.web.router.builder.RequestCondition.*;
import static io.micronaut.web.router.builder.ValueMatcher.*;

routes.GET("/search")
    .where(header("X-Beta").or(query("beta", equalTo("true"))))
    .order(-1)
    .handle(betaHandler);
routes.path("/admin", admin -> admin.where(peerAddress("10.0.0.0/8")));

A condition is data, not a predicate: only the router evaluates it, with the host and the client address as the server resolves them, see RequestCondition.Host and RequestCondition.RemoteAddress, and the clock of the application. Conditions combine with and(RequestCondition), or(RequestCondition) and negate(); a lambda is a custom(Predicate) condition.

A RequestCondition.Body condition, see body(Class, Predicate), is met by the body of the request: the server reads the body, from a copy, for the routes the request matched without it, and evaluates the body conditions last, see RequestCondition.Body. A body condition is a part every request of the route meets: a condition of a route or a group, or a part of all(RequestCondition...) or and(RequestCondition). It cannot be a part of any(RequestCondition...), or(RequestCondition) or negate(), which fail with an IllegalArgumentException.

5.3.0

    • remoteAddress

      static RequestCondition remoteAddress(String... cidrs)
      A request from a client address in one of the ranges, IPv4 or IPv6 in CIDR notation, e.g. remoteAddress("10.0.0.0/8", "192.168.1.7", "fd00::/8"): the address of the client as the server resolves it, see RequestCondition.RemoteAddress. An address without a prefix length is the range of that address alone. No name is ever looked up.

      The server resolves the address with its HttpClientAddressResolver, which trusts the X-Forwarded-For and Forwarded headers of the request unless micronaut.server.client-address-header is configured: a client can then send any address. Use it behind a trusted proxy that sets the configured header, and peerAddress(String...) for access control.

      Parameters:
      cidrs - The ranges of addresses, at least one
      Returns:
      The condition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a range is not a range of addresses

    • peerAddress

      static RequestCondition peerAddress(String... cidrs)
      A request whose connection comes from an address in one of the ranges, IPv4 or IPv6 in CIDR notation, e.g. peerAddress("10.0.0.0/8", "::1"): the address of the peer of the connection, HttpRequest.getRemoteAddress(), never a forwarded address, so a client cannot spoof it with a header. This is the condition for access control, e.g. an allow or deny list. Behind a proxy the peer is the proxy: see remoteAddress(String...) for the address of the client the proxy forwards. A request without a peer address, or whose peer address is unresolved, does not meet the condition. No name is ever looked up.
      Parameters:
      cidrs - The ranges of addresses, at least one
      Returns:
      The condition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a range is not a range of addresses

      static <T> RequestCondition.Body<T> body(Class<T> type, Predicate<? super T> predicate)

    • bodyAsync

      static <T> RequestCondition.Body<T> bodyAsync(Class<T> type, Function<? super T, ? extends CompletionStage<Boolean>> condition)
      A request whose body, decoded to the type, meets a condition decided later, e.g. after a lookup in a database: bodyAsync(Order.class, order -> customers.isPremiumAsync(order.customer())). The route is chosen once the stage completes, without blocking, and a stage that fails does not meet the condition, which is logged as a warning.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type
      Parameters:
      type - The type
      condition - The condition, which must not block: it returns a stage of whether the body meets it
      Returns:
      The condition
